task:
Create a focused repository-governance change that makes the PR acceptance rule canonical from now on. This is documentation/process enforcement only. Do not touch product behavior, Stage 27 implementation, V3/runtime/data work, deployment, production systems, CRE/CPE mechanics, Journal ingestion, or unrelated cleanup. Read CLAUDE.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, docs/development/chatgpt-ops-control-plane.md, and relevant existing policy-test patterns first.

Create one canonical policy document under docs/development/ (use a clear name such as pull-request-acceptance-policy.md), link it authoritatively from CLAUDE.md's working agreement, and update .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md so every PR records the latest-head acceptance evidence. Add a focused regression/contract test so this policy cannot silently disappear or regress to checking only one bot.

The canonical rule must state unambiguously:
1. No PR merges until every required CI/security/coverage/status check for the latest PR head has completed successfully. Green CI alone is insufficient.
2. Both configured automated reviewers — chatgpt-codex-connector (Codex Review) and Octopus Review — must have completed against the latest PR head before merge. Do not merge while either is pending, still reviewing, or errored. If a reviewer did not auto-run, explicitly trigger it and wait.
3. Inspect all relevant review surfaces with pagination: top-level PR/issue conversation comments, formal review bodies, inline review comments, and unresolved review conversations. Checking only a summary or only inline comments is insufficient.
4. Every substantive finding from either reviewer must be triaged against the actual latest code and recorded as one of: fixed and verified, demonstrated false positive with concrete evidence, superseded by a verified later change, or explicitly accepted risk by the repository owner. No substantive unresolved conversation may remain at merge.
5. A clean review from one bot never overrides a finding from the other.
6. Any new commit after a review invalidates that review for acceptance unless the reviewer clearly reviewed the new head; latest-head SHA must be recorded.
7. Reviewer service failure/unavailability is fail-closed by default. The only exception is an explicit written owner waiver on the PR that names the unavailable reviewer, records the replacement manual review/evidence, and accepts the risk; never infer or silently apply a waiver.
8. Late-arriving findings are prevented by waiting for completion; if a finding nevertheless arrives after merge, it enters the repair backlog immediately and blocks dependent work where relevant.

The PR template should include concise checkboxes/fields for latest head SHA, required checks, Codex status and reviewed SHA, Octopus status and reviewed SHA, inline/formal/top-level/unresolved-comment inspection, finding dispositions, and any explicit owner waiver. Keep it usable rather than bloated.

In CLAUDE.md, replace or supersede the current Codex-only merge-review wording with the canonical two-reviewer policy link. Preserve useful instructions about verifying bot claims rather than treating them as oracles, but remove ambiguity that Octopus is optional or that CI is sufficient. Do not alter the current roadmap/lane text in this task.

The regression test should structurally assert that the canonical document, CLAUDE.md link, and PR-template gate all require both Codex and Octopus, latest-head review, all review surfaces, no unresolved substantive findings, and fail-closed reviewer errors. Avoid brittle checks for an entire prose paragraph where targeted semantic markers are sufficient. Run the focused test, any relevant policy/hygiene tests, and git diff --check. End with changed files, test evidence, and any limitations. Do not merge or deploy.
